compression/read#

Consuming byte streams over caller-owned input and codecs.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let decoded = DecompressedReading(source, decompressor, 4096);
decoded.bytes(1024); // consumes output; source/codec stay caller-owned
decoded.close();    // closes only the adapter's private buffers

Description#

Consuming byte streams over caller-owned input and codecs. Constructors bind dependencies without reading/writing/finishing them; optional chunk_size is positive (InvalidArgument otherwise), default 8192. bytes(limit) requires a positive limit (InvalidReadLimit), returns at most that many bytes, retains excess output and never reads ahead while cached bytes remain.

Empty intermediate output batches do not signal EOF. Input is fed until output appears or the codec finishes; source EOF triggers finish(). Final batches are drained before stable EOF. An already finished codec is drained without source reads or a repeated finish. Decompressor remainder stays on the caller's codec. Short input reads are ordinary data; oversized reads are InvalidState.

Each finite output batch is fully cached, so memory is proportional to the largest pending batch plus the input chunk, not merely the requested limit. Concrete decompressors enforce their own cumulative output budget. Source/codec Errors propagate unchanged; after failure only close/closed work. Invalid read limits do not poison the adapter. close is idempotent; destroy releases owned buffers through the retained internal stream. No borrowed source or codec is closed. These streams do not implement iteration/cursors.

role CompressionFlow#

role CompressionFlow

A bound source-and-codec flow for the internal reader. The source is borrowed; input() consumes it and the remaining actions observe/drive the bound codec. These adapters preserve nominal Compressing/Decompressing distinctions and deliberately provide no close action. The fake echoes [1,2,255], delaying all output until finish; it is an isolated test double, not a wire codec.
